newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - FACTORS TO WATCH - AUG 11.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - FACTORS TO WATCH - AUG 11.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Monday:
* The Philippine equities market is likely to be wedged within a range as investors wait for currency and interest rate concerns to settle down, traders said.

* "We expect this range to prevail, at least until the cloud of uncertainty brought on by the regional currency turmoil blows over. Speculatives will continue to add spice to an otherwise defensive market," said a Sun Hung Kai Securities report.
* Anscor-Hagedorn Securities said the index will hover near 2,500.
* On Friday, the Philippine composite index closed 22.19 points lower at 2,647.82 points.
* The Dow Jones on Friday ended 156.78 points weaker at 8,031.22. PLDT's ADR closed lower by $0 1/2 at $32.
* The Philippine peso ended down at 28.51 to a U.S. dollar versus 28.46.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was at 18.0625 percent versus 18.09375 percent.

* A management committee will be formed to oversee the rehabilitation and operation of the financially-troubled Victorias Milling Co, a Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) officer said on Sunday.

* Fraudulent calls affected the first half earnings of mobile phone firm Pilipino Telephone Co, cutting its profit by 66 percent from the year-ago level, but analysts said it is still better than expected.
Piltel said its profits fell to 165.8 million in the first six months compared to 487.6 million in the same period last year.
* The Bankers Association of the Philippines (BAP) agreed to allow six foreign banks to participate again at the Philippine Dealing System from Monday, BAP president Deogracias Vistan said.
* Federal regulators have approved rules to slash the price of overseas phone calls in a move aimed at saving American consumers and businesses billions of dollars a year.

Federal Communications Comission chairman Reed Hundt predicted his agency's action will cut the average price of an international call from the United States to 20 cents a minute from the current 88 cents within five years.
* Philippine car sales in the first seven months of the year drop by 4.5 percent to 48,706 units from the year-ago 50,977, the Chamber of Automotive Manufacturers of the Philippines Inc said.

* Large outflows of much-needed capital and further weakening of the local currency will ensue should Congress push through with the lifting of the bank secrecy law and the imposition of tax on foreign currency deposits, central bank governor Gabriel Singson said. (MANILA BULLETIN/CHRONICLE)
* Newspaper BusinessWorld said the Philippines will further strengthen its fiscal position by improving revenue collection and cutting expenditures.
